page: Microsoft Azure M32-8ms is a memory-intensive virtual machine from the MS family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8280M processor with 8 dedicated vCPUs, 4 physical cores, and 2 threads per core. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz and includes a 105 MB L3 cache. This server is equipped with an exceptionally high memory capacity of 875.0 GB, yielding 109.38 GB of RAM per core. Additionally, it bundles a 1049 GB local SSD and is Premium Storage capable, though it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a clear tradeoff between massive memory capacity and processing performance. The CPU exhibits weak to poor performance across multiple tests, with a single-core stress-ng score of 1037.69 (bottom 10%) and a multi-core score of 5465.52 (bottom 25%). Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only large block speed of 38.73 GB/sec (bottom 25%) and a write large block speed of 31.04 GB/sec (middle 50%). Database operations on Passmark scored 2092.15, and Redis SET operations achieved 5.28 million operations per second, both falling into the bottom 25%. LLM inference speeds are also modest, with a 7B model text generation speed of 4.6 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance represents a specialized hardware profile where the budget is heavily allocated toward extreme memory density rather than raw compute power. The high RAM-to-vCPU ratio makes it a qualitative fit for workloads requiring massive in-memory datasets but relatively low CPU utilization. Appropriate workloads include large-scale in-memory databases, caching layers, and enterprise applications with massive memory footprints that do not require high-performance multi-threaded processing.
